path: 系统安全/Android/CVE-2024-43096 及更多：Android 安全更新中修复的关键 RCE 漏洞.md
revision_basis: Reassessment: the earlier blanket-conflict verdict was wrong. The article’s exact body segment at source line 65 names CVE-2024-43096, CVE-2024-43770, CVE-2024-43771, CVE-2024-49747, and CVE-2024-49748; the official Android January 2025 bulletin classifies each of these five System issues as RCE (official bulletin table, lines 100–104). The headline says “关键RCE” and “及更多,” while the bulletin distinguishes the remainder by type; this does not claim all eleven listed IDs are RCE. Earlier notes that lumped the additional EoP/DoS entries into the headline claim misread the scope. Existing editorial item 2 should be reconsidered as an overbroad-warning false positive. The official bulletin separately classifies CVE-2024-49724 and CVE-2023-40132 as EoP, CVE-2024-21464 and CVE-2024-20154/20146 as vendor entries without a bulletin type in that table, and CVE-2024-45558 as Qualcomm-sourced with no type column; these do not negate the five stated RCEs.

sources.finding: Official Android January 2025 bulletin, lines 100–104: the five IDs named in the article body each have Type RCE. Lines 105–113 classify additional System items separately, including EoP, ID and DoS.

path: 系统安全/Android/安卓音频解码组件曝高危漏洞，可致恶意代码执行，谷歌发布补丁.md
revision_basis: Reassessment: CNA’s short description of a decoder crash does not disprove the article’s Pixel-context RCE claim. Dolby’s original one-page UDC advisory identifies the issue as integer overflow, impact “Code Execution,” and CVSS 3.1 6.7 Medium; the PDF also says Pixel exploitation appears alongside other vulnerabilities and that other device classes most commonly crash/restart. Google Project Zero’s January 2026 Pixel research explicitly reports CVE-2025-54957 alone achieving arbitrary code execution in the Pixel 9 mediacodec/decoder context, with a separate CVE-2025-36934 used for kernel escalation; its later part says the Dolby bug is exploitable on its own for code execution in decoder context. Thus the headline RCE is substantiated, and the previous CNA-only contradiction was a false positive. Actual wording issues remain: source line 26 calls the vulnerability “高危” though Dolby rates it Medium (CVSS 6.7); editorial lines 41/47 attribute a “Pixel needs combination” proposition without clearly separating Dolby’s “alongside other vulnerabilities” note from Project Zero’s demonstrated standalone decoder-context RCE; “非Pixel” overgeneralizes Dolby’s “other device classes” wording. These differences affect severity and device scope, not whether RCE is possible on Pixel.

sources.finding: Official January 2026 Android bulletin is the patch context; not treated by itself as proof of exploit-chain details.
Google Project Zero reports CVE-2025-54957 used for arbitrary code execution in Pixel 9 mediacodec; a separate CVE-2025-36934 escalates from mediacodec to kernel.
Project Zero says CVE-2025-54957 is exploitable on its own for code execution in decoder context; the article does not equate that with standalone kernel compromise.

Downloaded original Dolby one-page advisory; SHA256 00bf7d84faed08630151e87beead1841911a29da173cd1f6becd687ed8b22f6d. It states Impact: Code Execution, CVSS 3.1 6.7 Medium, UDC 4.5–4.13, Pixel “alongside other vulnerabilities,” and other device classes most commonly crash/restart.

path: Web安全/邮件系统/Microsoft Exchange Server/Exchange 预授权 RCE ：CVE-2026-62911 深度剖析与企业级防御实战.md
revision_basis: Reassessment: the previous “correct to authorized EoP unless proven otherwise” conclusion was too strong. The CNA/MSRC record describes CVE-2026-62911 as authentication bypass/capture-replay leading to EoP, while the technical research describes a multi-step pre-auth chain: coerce a second Exchange server to authenticate, relay its machine-account NTLM handshake to another Exchange host, rely on the token-serialization right held by Exchange computer accounts, then write a file that can execute as SYSTEM. The MB VRED source states the relay cannot target the same server and applies only to multiple-Exchange-server setups (lines 165–167, 193–198); it also says these are demanding real-world conditions (204–210). Tachyon separately describes the CVE as one link in a three-bug chain ending in SYSTEM code execution (lines 25–27, 40–45), and explicitly distinguishes the vendor’s single-bug rating from chain outcome (line 70). Thus “pre-auth” can mean no prior user credential for the full relay chain and is compatible with the underlying EoP classification, though the article’s line 63 opening “only internal access” is incomplete without the relay/coercion and second-host prerequisites already captured in the editorial at lines 27 and 34. The evidence does not support flattening the merged CVE record into a standalone, unconstrained RCE.

sources.finding: Microsoft Security Response Center entry title classifies CVE-2026-62911 as Exchange Server Elevation of Privilege; the cached CNA values are retained in the linked evidence index.

Research lines 165–167 says only Exchange machine accounts have token-serialization right; lines 193–198 describes coercion and cross-host relay and states the captured hash cannot be relayed to the same server; lines 204–210 notes demanding conditions.

Lines 25–27 frame it as one link in a three-bug chain; lines 40–45 describe coercion, relay, authorization and file-write/execute steps; line 70 distinguishes standalone CVE rating from chain outcome.
